text:
Marathon Petroleum rose 0.42% today as oil prices continued climbing on Middle East tensions. Brent crude broke above $101 per barrel—the highest since May—driven by escalating U.S.-Iran conflict and concerns that supply disruptions could worsen. With refineries running at 98% capacity and oil storage at relatively lean levels, refiners like Marathon benefit when crude prices rise faster than they can pass costs to customers, improving their profit margins on each barrel processed.

The stock's 12.5% gain over two weeks tracks directly with the oil rally: Brent has surged roughly 10% in that span as geopolitical risk premium has built into energy markets. Refinery utilization staying near maximum suggests the industry is running hard to meet demand, and with Middle East tensions keeping a floor under crude prices, that elevated profitability environment is likely supporting the sector broadly.
